51101176.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to Plasmodium falciparum HSP90 nucleotide binding domain by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.SPR Analysis: 4.3.8.2. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) analysis. SPR measurements were performed on a Biacore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare) at 25 °C. Purified PfHsp90 and PfGRP94 nucleotide binding domains were immobilized on a CM5 sensor chip using NHS/EDC coupling following the manufacturer protocol to levels of 3,000 and 7,000 resonance units, respectively, and reference surfaces without immobilized proteins served as a control for nonspecific binding and refractive index changes. Seven different concentrations of the compounds between 0.4 nM and 1 mM were injected in triplicate over the sensor chip at 30 μL/min in random order. The running buffer was 10 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 0.005% P20, 1% DMSO and 2 mM MgCl2. Buffer-only injections were used as blanks. All dissociation constants were estimated using double-subtracted sensorgrams using BioEvaluation software (GE Healthcare). The relative responses recorded during the last 5 s of each injection were used to estimate the equilibrium constant, and these values were used to estimate the dissociation constant (Kd). A steady-state affinity analysis was used as implemented in BioEvaluation software.
original_paragraph.Figure 6 caption: Fig. 6. Compound 1* reduce the number of oocysts in midgut of A. stephensi. Number of oocysts of PbGFP in midgut of A. stephensi (n = 60 per group) was quantified using fluorescence microscopy. (A) Scatter dot plot showed number of oocysts per mosquito; black line represents median with interquartile range; (B) Bars plot showed mean ± SD number of oocysts per group of treatment. Data are expressed as mean ± SD ***p < 0.001.
